nodes.long_description:
Nanome 2.0 marks a revolutionary advance in molecular design and simulation. This new iteration is not just an upgrade; it is a complete overhaul with a brand-new architecture that enhances every aspect of the user experience. This version brings a faster, more stable, and deeply intuitive platform for molecular exploration. We’ve refined the user interface to include an improved web portal with drag-and-drop support for PDB, MMCIF, and SDF file formats, ensuring seamless transitions from web to VR. The VR interface itself is meticulously designed for effortless scene navigation and precise molecule manipulation.

In terms of molecule management, users can now load and visualize multiple formats, organize molecules within customizable workspaces, and manage scenes with advanced control over molecule positions and scaling. Apply both default and custom visual representations like Ball & Stick, Van Der Waals, Wire, Cartoon, and Surface to suit various analytical needs.

Collaboration is smoother than ever with basic features that allow joining via a code, viewing a list of collaborators in a workspace, and engaging in multi-user manipulation of molecules without a presenter mode. Our collaboration awareness tools ensure that users share workspaces efficiently, maintaining visibility through transparent avatars and allowing independent scene navigation.

Experience the future of molecular XR today with Nanome 2.0 Beta on App Lab and contribute to shaping this cutting-edge platform
nodes.short_description: Nanome 2.0 represents a paradigm shift in molecular design and simulation. With a completely revamped architecture, this version not only introduces a suite of innovative features but also enhances the core functionalities that users loved in version 1. The result is a faster, more stable, and incredibly intuitive platform for exploring the molecular world. This beta version now available on App Lab, allows users to test and provide feedback on the new features of Nanome 2.0.

nodes.change_log:
New Features and Improvements

- Comments: discuss annotations, scenes, or the whole workspace in threaded comments with replies, @mentions, emoji reactions, watched threads, and unread indicators, all updated live. Annotations and comments now share one menu, and a comment's atom chip highlights and zooms to the atoms it refers to.
- Pocket minimization in the Ligand Builder: pick a receptor, choose rigid receptor, flexible pocket, or flexible side chains, set a pocket radius, then minimize the ligand in place. Results report energy plus ligand and pocket RMSD, and runs can be cancelled or undone. Ligands that contain metal atoms cannot be minimized.
- Ligand Builder attachment points now follow each atom's valence and geometry. Bring a fragment to an attachment point to preview it, twist it around the bond with snapping to favorable torsions, and release to attach; rings close automatically. A new Auto Relax button cleans up nearby geometry after each edit.
- Ligand Builder Replace mode can fuse a fragment onto a ring, merging every overlapping atom, with an aromatic preview.
- New procedurally generated mountain skyboxes in each theme's colors, making the Quest download about 30 MB smaller. Skybox themes and night mode also come to the web viewer.
- New atom and bond rendering: spheres and cylinders are drawn as smooth, antialiased GPU impostors at any zoom, with much higher frame rates on large structures. Applies to structures being edited, selection highlights, and the web viewer.
- Desktop and web viewer: hover and click atoms, bonds, and residues to highlight and select them, click atoms to measure distances and angles, and double-click to zoom to a residue or entry. Rotation and zoom pivot on the selection or the highlighted residue under the cursor.
- The default pointer now highlights whole residues. Pull the trigger (or click) to add the hovered residue to the selection or remove it.
- In XR, your off-hand always works as a pointer for hovering and selecting atoms, whatever tool the other hand holds.
- In XR, pointing at an interaction, measurement, or text annotation shows a tooltip with its details, such as interaction type, distance, and the two groups involved.
- When you follow someone, you now see their current tool and mode, the atoms they hover and select, and their in-progress edits (ligand building, torsions, rotamers) live before they commit them.
- Following someone who is following another user takes you to the person at the end of the chain, and your view smoothly re-aligns to what the leader is looking at.
- Hide and show text, sound, and image annotations with an eye toggle on each row, or all at once with Hide All / Show All, instead of deleting them.
- Structure alignment now runs on the server, with a choice of CE-Align or TM-Align. Aligning trajectory entries keeps their current frame instead of jumping to frame 0.
- Residue editing can score rotamer clashes and hydrogen bonds against visible atoms only or against all atoms.
- Residue editing: add residues with the controller while in rotamer mode, and selected residues are grouped by entry in a scrollable list.
- Components have a new Delete Atoms action to permanently remove their atoms from a structure, with a confirmation.
- Distance components can include atoms from all entries in the workspace, and have a new 'Include ligands' option (off by default).
- Components menu: hover a component to see its atom count, empty components are grayed out, and entries hidden by the performance limiter are marked, with a shortcut to the limiter settings.
- Clash markers scale in size and brightness with how much the atoms overlap.
- Metal coordination detection now includes methionine sulfur, iron-sulfur cluster sulfides, and aromatic nitrogen donors such as porphyrin and imidazole rings.
- Web viewer can create and remove interaction components (polymer-ligand, polymer-polymer, and chain-chain).
- The Sequences menu has a 'Filter hidden structures' toggle to show only structures currently displayed.
- Covalently bound ligands now keep their bond to the protein. Modified residues with an attached group are split into the standard amino acid, kept in the protein, and the attached group, treated as a ligand.
- Molecular surfaces are generated at higher resolution for smoother, more detailed surfaces.
- New workspaces get a default 'Workspace N' name, and an empty workspace with a default name is renamed after the first structure loaded into it.
- Teammates' online status, workspace invites, and join requests update instantly, including for colleagues in the web viewer.
- Export scene analysis data as a ZIP of CSV files covering chemical interactions, measurements, and minimization history.
- AI assistant (MCP) tools can read a summary of each workspace's contents, such as chains, residue ranges, ligands, and ions.
- Free licenses now have limits: 1 owned project, 3 owned workspaces, 5 structures per workspace, and view-only access to shared workspaces and projects, with clear messages when a limit is hit.
- Nanome warns you when your license expires within 30 days, and signs you out with a clear notice when it expires.
- Sign-in errors now explain what went wrong, such as wrong credentials, an account that must use Google, Microsoft, Apple, or SSO sign-in, an organization IP restriction, or a network problem.
- Switching scenes during a recording now asks for confirmation, then stops the recording and switches, keeping the recording on the scene where it was made.
- The Projects, Workspaces, Ligands, and rotamer lists use a new shared table with column sorting (also while searching), a loading indicator, and an empty-state message.
- Press Escape to show or hide the main menu in desktop mode.
- In XR, press X on your off-hand controller (left by default) to mute or unmute your microphone.
- Smaller touches: the Scenes menu scrolls to the active scene, the menu lock button turns yellow while locked, and saving an edited ligand as a new entry keeps its chemical property annotations.

Optimizations and Fixes

- Smoother model and trajectory playback: upcoming frames are precomputed in the background, and interactions, annotations, and residue labels stay visible and update during playback.
- Molecular dynamics trajectories load faster and use much less storage and server memory.
- Faster, more accurate loading of MD files: large GROMACS (.gro) systems load far faster, GRO files split into chains when residue numbering restarts, secondary structure skips water and solvent, and terminal caps (ACE, NME, NH2) stay part of the protein.
- Faster loading with more accurate bonds and formal charges for structures containing DNA or RNA.
- Ligand bonding for PDB and mmCIF files now comes from the RCSB Chemical Component Dictionary, and metal coordination is no longer drawn as covalent bonds.
- Structures with very large ligands no longer stall while loading, files no longer fail when secondary structure cannot be computed, and some mmCIF files no longer report a spurious bond-table error.
- File loading errors show a short readable message instead of a stack trace.
- Cancelling a load or leaving a workspace while a large structure is rendering no longer freezes the app, and several other freeze risks are removed.
- The Components menu stays responsive in large workspaces, and opening the Sequence menu no longer stalls the app.
- Residue editing is faster: rotamer suggestions calculate much faster in large workspaces, and applying edits no longer makes the structure flash.
- Faster model updates on large structures, and fewer frame hitches while hovering and editing with the Builder.
- Fewer per-frame memory allocations from avatar and pointer tracking, reducing garbage-collection stutter.
- Scenes with image, sound, or recording annotations load and save faster.
- Bonds, interactions, distance selections, and secondary structure are no longer missed in very dense structures.
- Committing edits that remove atoms bonded to atoms outside the edited region, such as residue edits on residues with alternate locations, no longer causes errors.
- Ligand Builder: aromaticity is recalculated after every edit, undoing to an empty ligand no longer gets stuck, invalid bond clicks are ignored, switching workspaces fully resets the Builder, and stray white pixels no longer appear in the fragment list.
- Minimization now uses the hydrogenated molecule for its force field, and the fragment labelled 'Acid Anhydride' is now correct.
- Residue editing keeps showing earlier unapplied mutations and rotamers when you edit another residue, and shows a message when rotamer calculation fails or times out.
- Components: a component no longer disappears when one of several atomistic representations is hidden, components spanning several entries no longer vanish, and the menu refreshes after an entry is edited.
- The 'Ignore selection' option for distance components now excludes the selected atoms, and measuring between the same atom in two models no longer causes errors.
- Rendering: cartoon highlights line up with the correct residue, surface and wireframe colors are no longer washed out, and selection highlights no longer stick or ghost during playback.
- Wireframe boxes and hover highlights no longer get stuck after hovering items in menus.
- Sound annotations that reach the 5-minute limit are no longer lost, and the recorder shows elapsed and maximum time with a warning at the limit.
- Annotations on atoms shown only as ribbon are no longer hidden, text and voice note popups open in front of you after you turn, and the '/' in sound playback time displays correctly.
- Spotlight: people who join or reconnect mid-session follow the presenter automatically, followers resume when the presenter reconnects, a briefly disconnected presenter returns as the same participant, and web viewers start following without a 6-second delay.
- Following resumes after your headset wakes from sleep, recentering keeps you aligned with the leader, and the view no longer jitters when the leader turns quickly.
- Microphone buttons are disabled with an explanation when microphone permission is denied, and the session reconnects after losing access to a workspace instead of staying offline until restart.
- Waking your headset or rejoining a busy session no longer plays a burst of overlapping join and leave sounds.
- Permission changes, including accepted join requests, apply immediately for people already in the workspace.
- Workspaces: a workspace sent from the web opens reliably on app start, a workspace joined by code appears right away on your other devices, the list sorts by last opened correctly, and a mistyped workspace code shows a clear error.
- Workspaces opened from a share link or code show their project name instead of 'Unknown Project'.
- A failed scene load no longer leaves the scene display stuck until restart.
- Surface controls are disabled with an explanation during playback, and surface changes received during playback apply when it stops.
- The interactions count in the representations popup now includes halogen-pi interactions.
- Long multi-line text fields and the VR keyboard preview now scroll instead of growing without limit, and the scene options button no longer appears in the collapsed Scenes menu.
- Wrist menu buttons no longer intermittently stop responding.

Nanome v2.6.0

New Features and Improvements

* Scene Recording & Playback: record scenes (including their annotations) and play them back, including on the web viewer.
* Residue Editor: one built-in tool for both protein residue mutations and rotamer (side-chain) edits. 
* MARA Tools: run MARA cheminformatics tools on a whole entry, a component, or your current selection right from the in-headset sidebar (VR + desktop); results and any molecular outputs come back as new structures without changing what you sent.
* Rich Annotations: add custom text and sound annotations, with URLs supported inside text.
* Ligand Table View Presets: save and switch ligand-table layouts per Project, filter by numeric rating, and toggle a 3D tag per ligand.
* Shared Selection: opt-in sharing of your selection with collaborators in your avatar color; following a user now shows their selection too.
* XR Keyboard v2: real-time dictation and clipboard support in the in-headset keyboard.
* Interactions: halogen-π interactions, ligand↔protein-only filtering, highlighting that networks across users, and show/hide toggles for pinned interaction labels, zoom on interactions.
* Multi-model & trajectory: load multi-model MAE files, atom-count-aware frame limits, smoother large-trajectory playback, and per-frame surfaces when stepping through frames.
* More new tools: Export to Smiles, direct distance filters, a redesigned color picker, server switch (private cloud / on-prem), and a Loading Report that flags and auto-resolves fixable load issues.
* Pointer highlight: flash a highlight around your pointer that broadcasts to collaborators so they can see where you're pointing.
* Web App: sequence menu, multi-protein structure alignment, image export, scene-playback controls, .pdbqt loading, touch input for tablets and phones, Org role management, and structures now render visible on load. Viewers can step through models and make selections.

Optimizations and Fixes

* Rebuilt real-time collaboration networking: replaced Photon with a custom in-house networking stack for more reliable multi-user sessions. Foundational and invisible by design, it underpins all live collaboration going forward.
* Large workspaces: level-of-detail rendering, a dynamic-resolution spatial grid, and faster large-molecule loading, with rendering improvements for Quest and Android.
* Surfaces: surface and ESP computation now runs asynchronously in the background so it no longer stalls the session, plus a faster surface protocol and correct surfaces for disconnected atoms (waters, ions).
* Networking efficiency: more efficient payload compression for large structures.
* Network health: live high-ping indicators and better connection-loss recovery in both XR and web.
* Performance safeguards: the load manager that hides very heavy structures to protect framerate now correctly counts passthrough and editable-model rendering against its budget.
* Loading: cancellable structure loading with a progress bar, and a fix for loads that stalled on unknown workspaces.
* Stability: eliminated multiple API and main-thread freezes (selection builder, menu scroll, workspace change) and cleaned up connection, token.
* Web App reliability: fixed the ~30-second disconnect/rejoin loop that occurred while a tab was backgrounded.
* 60+ additional fixes across freezes, UI polish, workspace management, and rendering, plus a higher scene limit (now 50 per workspace) and faster, more accurate ring detection.

Nanome v2.5.1 Release Notes

Summary

* WebGL instanced rendering: Real-time playback of 20,000+ atom MD trajectories on WebGL with dramatically lower memory use.
* Torsion angle tool: Haptic feedback, cleaner menu, fixed stale state, and faster editing.
* Skybox selection: Choose VR backgrounds and toggle the ground plane from settings.
* Stepper controls: Precise numeric inputs replace sliders on Distance Filter and Electrostatic Ramp panels.
* Networked focus on WebGL: See teammates' highlight focus in shared workspaces from the WebGL client.
* Trajectory stability: General optimizations for Multi-model entries.
* Crash & hang fixes: Resolved hang-on-exit (notably Windows) and a native crash in the ribbon builder.


New Features

* WebGL instanced atomistic rendering: Large structures and 20,000+ atom MD trajectories now play back in real time on WebGL with dramatically reduced memory use.
* Skybox selection: A new settings dropdown lets users pick VR background environments and toggle ground plane visibility.
* Stepper controls: Distance Filter and Electrostatic Ramp panels replace sliders with numeric input + hold-to-repeat steppers for precise XR adjustment.

Improvements

* Torsion haptics: VR controllers now vibrate as the torsion angle changes for a more tactile sense of conformational adjustment.
* Torsion menu cleanup: Empty structures are now hidden from the torsion tool menu.
* Torsion performance: Significant performance improvements during active torsion editing.
* Trajectory stability: Optimized trajectory network usage.
* Frame navigation tooltips: Previous/Next Frame buttons now show tooltips in the trajectory panel.
* Structure group auto-expand/collapse: Groups now expand when shown and collapse when hidden, matching the web UI.
* Project permission label: Project permission level is now shown as a label, and the options menu is disabled for non-editable roles.
* Camera follow pitch offset: Following another user now correctly accounts for pitch offset.
* WebGL memory: Increased RAM allocation for the WebGL client to support larger sessions.
* Recenter Self countdown: Improved sound and increased volume for better feedback.

Bug Fixes

* Hang on exit: Resolved an application hang on close for Windows clients.
* Ribbon builder crash: Fixed a native memory crash in the ribbon secondary-structure builder.
* Public workspace permissions: Fixed permission issues with workspaces marked as public.
* Stale invitation status: Workspace invitation status labels now clear correctly after a member leaves.
* Torsion strain toggle: The torsion strain toggle now stays in sync with tool state across re-entry.
* Torsion stale visuals: Fixed stale highlight colors and atom positions persisting after exiting the torsion tool.
* Torsion calculation errors: Fixed angle calculation errors in the torsion tool.
* Structure alignment errors: Resolved potential errors during structure alignment operations.
* Controller menu init: Fixed menu initialization and re-initialization issues affecting the controller tool menu.
* Web App Rendering: Fixed annotation, interaction, and focus highlighting on on Web App.

v2.5.0 Release Notes

Overview

v2.5.0 marks Nanome's transition from Early Access (v2.4) to a production-ready release — built for teams and enterprise deployment. This release adds the access controls, permission systems, and licensing enforcement needed for real-world multi-user environments, alongside major new scientific tools and cross-platform collaboration.
Key themes:

* Enterprise readiness — projects, workspace permissions, enforced license types, concurrent session limits
* New scientific tools — torsion angle manipulation, trajectory playback, interaction analysis
* Web + XR collaboration — web viewers now connect to the same real-time session as Quest users (previously isolated). Scientists can collaborate across devices for the first time.
* Stability — 30+ bug fixes, rendering pipeline improvements, and a more reliable cross-platform foundation

Features TL;DR

* Torsion Angle Tool — interactively rotate dihedral angles with real-time strain coloring
* Trajectory Playback — load and scrub molecular dynamics frame-by-frame, synced across users (2,000 frame limit)
* Web ↔ XR Collaboration — web and Quest users now share the same live session with cursors, voice, and real-time sync
* Projects & Permissions — project-based workspace organization with owner/editor/viewer access, public sharing, and session concurrency limits
* Interaction Analysis — visualize, annotate, and report on chemical interactions with hover highlighting
* New File Formats — load MAE, PSE/MOE, PQR as entries into existing workspaces, plus improved PDB parsing
* User Focus Mode — highlight and focus on specific users or components with persistent visual emphasis
* Scene Management — save/restore point-of-view per scene, apply transforms across scenes, recenter view
* Electrostatic Surface Potential (ESP) Maps — custom ESP color ramps with adjustable scales, synced across users in real-time

Fixes & Improvements TL;DR

* 30+ bug fixes across rendering, controllers, workspace management, tools, and networking
* Performance — persistent surface caching (including WebGL — surfaces load instantly on revisit), surface computation fixes, rendering improvements


New Features

Torsion Angle Tool

Interactively rotate dihedral angles in molecular structures. Strain is visualized in real-time as a green→yellow→red atom coloring gradient (low to high strain), with a total strain value displayed numerically in the menu. Toggle between whole-structure or local (near the edited bond) strain views. Select which structure to edit from the torsion menu, with fast-trigger prevention for invalid rotations.

Trajectory Playback

Load and play back molecular dynamics trajectories frame-by-frame with optimized networking and UI controls. Includes frame compression, synchronized playback across users, and trajectory frame positioning in scenes. Current limit: 2,000 frames per trajectory (balances usability with Quest device memory). Streaming and indexing for larger trajectories planned for next release.

Projects & Workspace Management

Complete overhaul of workspace and project organization with shared workspaces, permission controls (owner/editor/viewer), public workspaces with anonymous access, and XR device concurrency limits (max 2 sessions). Includes project creation with workspace assignment and owner-based access controls.

Interaction Analysis & Annotation

Visualize and annotate chemical interactions between molecular components with interactive menus and hover highlighting. Includes interaction report generation, annotation rendering, and SDF file support.

User Focus Mode

Click on a molecular component to focus it with a persistent color highlight. Click again to defocus. Works on ribbons, atoms, and DNA chains. Hidden entries, groups, and components are dimmed for visual clarity.

Scene Management & POV

Save and restore point-of-view per scene within a workspace. Apply component transformations (position, rotation, scale) and visibility changes consistently across multiple scenes via "Apply Across Scenes" UI. Recenter view with confirmation overlay. Save user's last viewed scene per workspace for convenient session resumption.

Molecular File Format Support

MAE, PSE, and MOE files can now be loaded as new entries into existing workspaces (previously only supported as new workspace creation via web). MOE files now parse per-atom/residue/chain representations to recreate the original visualization. Added PQR file format support — a whitespace-delimited PDB variant used by APBS for electrostatic potential calculations (stores charge and radius per atom). Improved PDB parsing for shorter/flexible line formats.

Electrostatic Surface Enhancements

Custom ESP color ramps with adjustable scales that sync across users in real-time. Full-surface electrostatic coloring and PQR file format support for electrostatic potential calculations.

Web App (MARA)

Cross-platform (Unity ↔ Web)

* Real-time Web ↔ XR collaboration — web users now join the same live Photon session as Quest/PCVR users. See each other's cursors, hear voice chat, and view molecular changes in real-time. Previously, web and XR were completely isolated experiences.
* Workspace UI overhaul — new panel layout with Scenes, Entries (Components), MARA, and Import panels
* Trajectory playback on web — play/pause/scrub molecular dynamics with synced controls
* Public workspace access — anonymous users can view shared workspaces without login
* Zoom to components — click to zoom on individual molecular components
* Improved trackball controls — better mouse-based rotation and navigation
* VoIP reconnection — handle stale tab audio connections after inactivity

New in MARA

* Workspace Viewer — completely redesigned workspace viewing experience with new layout and navigation
* Workspace Chat — chat with other users directly inside workspaces
* Pinned Chats — pin important chat messages for easy reference
* User Focus & Follow — follow another user's viewpoint in real-time from the web viewer
* Viewer Avatars — see other users' avatars in the workspace viewer
* Projects & Permissions — create and manage projects, assign workspaces, and control owner/editor/viewer access from the web
* Move Workspaces between Projects — drag or move workspaces into different projects
* Public Workspaces — share workspaces with anonymous public access — no login required to view
* Electron Desktop App — optional desktop wrapper for a native app experience
* CSV Export from AI Tables — download data tables from MARA AI responses as CSV files

MARA Improvements

* Deploy without AI — web UI can now be deployed without the AI assistant for enterprise environments
* Paginated Tools — tool browsing page now paginates for better navigation
* Viewer Responsiveness — improved layout on mobile and tablet screens
* Better Clarification Prompts — improved "Ask for Clarification" flow in AI interactions
* Smarter Tool Suggestions — AI assistant encourages use of CSV tools when appropriate
* Faster Workspace Loading — uses batch loading route for workspace entries

MARA Fixes

* Fixed environment variable slowdown and enterprise build issues
* Fixed workspace ID handling
* Fixed chat attachment display
* Disabled caching on index.html to prevent stale deployments
* Fixed enterprise tool server connectivity
* Made tool errors visible to users for easier debugging
* Fixed quote escaping and SMILES/SMARTS backtick handling in AI responses
* Fixed streaming broken by gzip compression

Improvements

* Persistent surface caching (including WebGL) — molecular surfaces are cached and load instantly on revisit instead of recomputing from scratch. A major performance improvement for workflows involving repeated surface inspection
* Customizable pocket size for binding site analysis
* Ribbon selection with visual highlighting
* Zoom and pan on individual molecular components
* Duplicate ligand/chain/component as new entry
* Position molecule representation for duplicated entries
* Show surface loading indicators on component items
* Improved PDB atom element detection from residue names
* Added nucleic acid atom support for ribbon selection
* Handedness support for XR controllers
* Handedness-aware controller grab mechanics and rotation handling
* Improved joystick and scroll input responsiveness
* Passthrough camera support on PC VR devices
* REST API endpoint for loading DX maps
* Increased file upload size limits
* Enhanced tooltip and dropdown z-sorting
* Consolidated user event subscriptions for better performance
* Better trackball controls — center rotation on entry
* Reset active tool state on tool change
* WebGL microphone permission handling and WebSocket security


Bug Fixes

Rendering & Visualization

* Fixed CIF file loading
* Fixed surface computation lag and concurrent execution issues
* Fixed GRO file loading issues

Controllers & Input

* Fixed controller rotation and grab mechanics

Workspace & Project Management

* Fixed workspace loading freeze and infinite cancel loop
* Fixed unexpected workspace movement
* Fixed workspace update synchronization on scene changes

Tools & Features

* Fixed molecular alignment threading
* Fixed selection tool highlight persistence

UI & Menus

* Fixed stop follow UI state

Web & Networking

* Fixed Photon recorder threading and voice implementation
* Fixed error handling when sending data fails
* Fixed RCSB PDB download stream closure error

API & Backend

* Fixed API routing retry
* Fixed API stability issues
* Fixed PostgreSQL collation version warning

Core Stability

* Fixed LobbyProtein position

Known Issues

* Performance regression — frame rate drops observed in scenes with many visible molecular surfaces; investigating surface rendering pipeline optimization
* Trajectory freeze — trajectory playback can freeze when scrubbing rapidly near the end of long trajectories (1,500+ frames)
* Follow desync — "Follow" mode can desync between web and XR users under high-latency network conditions, causing the follower's viewpoint to lag or jump
